card.name: Chobi
card.tagline: Iraq's popular hand-holding line dance of weddings
card.profile: Chobi (also Choubi, Choby, Jawbi) is the most popular Iraqi group/line dance, performed at weddings and celebrations with dancers holding hands shoulder-to-shoulder in a half-circle led by a performer holding a rosary or knotted handkerchief to mark the rhythm (Fanack). Compiler Mark Gergis (Sublime Frequencies) describes it as 'Iraq's version of the regionally popular dabke, another celebratory Levantine folkloric style of rhythm and line dance,' driven by the distinctive crisp percussion of the khishba (zanbour, Arabic for 'wasp') hand-drum, alongside oud, fiddles, double-reed instruments and keyboards (Sublime Frequencies). Danced by Arabs, Kurds, Assyrians and other Iraqi communities, it is unofficially called the national dance of Iraq (Sublime Frequencies). The EN Wikipedia article is titled 'Jawbi.'
card.insight: Once an all-male display of manhood and tribal strength, chobi is now danced by everyone at weddings; it appears on Iraq's national intangible cultural heritage inventory (Jawbi, Wikipedia; Fanack).
